subject: Intermittent request backlog & error uplift — exec sync
messages:
From: Jordan Leary <jordan@brightline.com>

Cc: Brightline SaaSOps <saas-ops@brightline.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden spike in error rate + long queues this morning

Hey Mateo,

Quick heads-up — between ~08:45 and 09:00 PT we saw a batch of customer checkout flows hit 10–15s response times and about a 3% error rate (usually <0.1%). The spike coincided with a wave of concurrent requests from a marketing campaign; we sent a sample of failing payloads to SaaSOps.

Attached: brightline_error_sample.json (errors & IDs).

Can your team confirm whether this is a capacity/concurrency limit or something else (routing/backpressure)? This is starting to impact live payments — can loop in our account exec if useful.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Product Manager, Brightline

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:26:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Sudden spike in error rate + long queues this morning

Forwarding Brightline report — raising to ops and eng for triage. Jordan includes a small sample of failing request IDs.

Ben/Laura — please triage the following ASAP:
- Are their requests getting queued because of concurrency caps on the Dedicated pool or due to a fanout pattern?
- Any KV cache pressure or prefix-cache churn?
- Confirm whether the 504s are our gateway timing out or upstream service errors.

If this is confirmed as backpressure, propose a temporary mitigation (short throttle, burst cap increase, or drain). We need a one-paragraph status for execs within the hour.

Mateo Alvarez
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden spike in error rate + long queues this morning

Thanks for the ping — triage notes below (quick, live):

What I see so far:
- Alerting captured a surge in queued requests on the Brightline Dedicated pool starting 08:42 PT; concurrent inflight reached the pool concurrency cap for ~90s.
- Long-tail latency correlates with a minority of requests that have large prompt sizes (~3–4x avg token count) which increases compute per-request and blocks GPU slots in our serving runtime.
- Error samples in the attachment show 504s (gateway timeout) + a small fraction of 5xxs from the runtime OOMing on one older node. Node OOMs likely due to outlier prompt sizes combined with concurrent KV cache pressure.

Immediate mitigations proposed (short window):
1) Apply a temporary request size guard for Brightline to reject >2.5x avg prompt with 413 + guidance (safe, low-friction).
2) Allow one-time +25% burst of concurrency for Brightline's dedicated pool for 10 minutes to absorb the marketing wave.
3) Kick an emergency drain of the oldest queued requests (per runbook) to free KV cache and reduce QoS inversion.

I can push (2) now if Mateo signs off — will coordinate with infra to monitor p95/p99 and error rate.

Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden spike in error rate + long queues this morning

Quick update for exec note:
- Confirmed queueing is driven primarily by concurrency caps on the Brightline Dedicated pool + a handful of oversized requests (~3% of traffic) that exceed our typical runtime slices and cause head-of-line blocking.
- KV cache churn visible on two older nodes; memory pressure triggered an OOM on one node (we're patching that node config).

Actions taken:
- Ben increased burst concurrency by 25% for 10m at 09:52 PT — resulted in immediate reduction in queue depth. Monitoring shows p95 back down to normal, p99 improved but still elevated for ~5 outlier requests.
- Applied a soft-size-check at the gateway that returns a 413 with link to guidance for oversized payloads (deployed 10:00 PT).
- Started a coordinated node recycle on the problematic node; infra to replace with patched config (ETA 30m).

Attachments: queue_drain_runbook.md (runbook used for drain).

Need for exec brief: one-slide summary (cause, impact, mitigation, next steps). Mateo — can you authorize me to escalate this into a 10m exec sync if Jordan's team sees more impact? I can prepare the slide.

Laura Bennett
Head of Production Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Leary <jordan@brightline.com>, Brightline SaaSOps <saas-ops@brightline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Sudden spike in error rate + long queues this morning

Jordan — quick exec-style summary and next steps (short):

1) What happened: a burst of concurrent traffic from a marketing campaign produced a cluster of oversized prompts (~3% of requests) locking GPU slots and causing head-of-line blocking. One older node hit memory pressure and OOMed, generating a small number of 5xxs; the gateway returned 504s for several requests waiting in queue.

2) Impact: short-lived (09:52–10:02 PT) increase in p99 and ~3% error rate for affected requests; business-critical checkout flows were impacted for a small subset of customers. We have not seen ongoing errors since mitigation.

3) Mitigation completed: temporary +25% burst capacity applied; soft gateway size guard deployed; problematic node recycled with patched memory settings; queue drain executed. See attached ops_brief_for_exec.pdf for the slide used in the postmortem.

4) Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Engineering (Ben): add a production-side input size histogram, and add an automated outlier routing policy to divert oversized requests to a buffered path (ETA 2w).
- Ops (Laura): include Brightline in a targeted pre-warming experiment for predictable campaigns (ETA 1w).
- Account (Mateo): propose a documentation note for Brightline with recommended request sizing and traffic shaping.

We’re keeping a close eye; please re-open if you see any recurrence. Happy to set a 10m exec sync if you want to review the one-slide brief.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
